slides.title: How can I express what I think about an issue?
slides.body: Let's learn how to write a for/against essay.
slides.notes: Ask: What do you think this lesson is about? Point at the angel and devil on the splash.

slides.title: Why is this lesson important?
slides.body:
• Every day, people argue for and against things.
  • A clear opinion makes your writing powerful.
  • Essays and exams ask for your opinion.
slides.notes: Frame: phones, apps, and school rules all have two sides. Both sides matter.

slides.title: Pair Talk
slides.body:
What technology do you use every day?

What is good about it? What is bad about it?

Tell your partner. Give one reason.

Opinion — Reason — Evidence
slides.notes: Pairs discuss for two minutes. Timer starts automatically. Elicit: an opinion needs a reason.

slides.title: The writing task
slides.body:
Page 132

Write an essay about a kind of technology.

Give the advantages and disadvantages.

End with your opinion.

Say if you are for or against it.
slides.notes: Read the task aloud. Ask: What are the three parts?

slides.title: Strategy: Understand the task
slides.body:
DoRead the task twice.
WhyEvery task has three parts.
HowFind the topic. See both sides. Plan your opinion.
slides.notes: Model reading the task aloud twice. Point at each part.

slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 1

QuestionWhat do you have to do in the essay?
AnswerGive the advantages and the disadvantages. End with your opinion.
ExplanationThe task needs both sides, then your opinion.
Transcript"state if you are for or against using this kind of technology"
slides.notes: Click each row. Stress: both sides, then your opinion.

slides.title: The model essay has four parts
slides.body:
IntroductionAsks the question.
Paragraph 2The advantages.
Paragraph 3The disadvantages.
ConclusionYour opinion. For or against.
slides.notes: Point at each paragraph on page 132. Read the model essay together.

slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 2

QuestionWhich topic is the essay about?
AnswerStreaming music.
ExplanationThe model compares streaming music with downloads.
Transcript"How do you listen to music?"
slides.notes: The essay answers the question in the first line.

slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 2

QuestionIs the writer for or against the topic? Why?
AnswerAgainst. The writer prefers downloads.
ExplanationThey think it is better to own the music you love.
Transcript"That's why overall, I still prefer downloads."
slides.notes: The writer shows both sides, then chooses one in the conclusion.

slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 3

QuestionHow many paragraphs are there?
AnswerFour.
ExplanationAn introduction, two main paragraphs, and a conclusion.
Transcript"So what are the advantages and disadvantages of doing this?"
slides.notes: Point at the four paragraphs in the book.

slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 3

QuestionHow does the writer begin paragraphs 2 and 3?
AnswerParagraph 2: "Let's start with the advantages." Paragraph 3: "Turning to the disadvantages, ..."
ExplanationClear openings tell the reader what comes next.
Transcript"Turning to the disadvantages, ..."
slides.notes: These openings will become key phrases in lesson 3.

slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 3

QuestionHow many advantages are described in paragraph 2?
AnswerFour advantages.
ExplanationListen anywhere. Make playlists. Find new music. Stream for free.
Transcript"Finally, it's possible to stream music for free, which is great for young people."
slides.notes: Students find the four advantages in the book first.

slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 3

QuestionHow many disadvantages are described in paragraph 3?
AnswerFour disadvantages.
ExplanationYou need good Wi-Fi. The service can cost money. Audio quality can be poor. You do not own the music.
Transcript"when you stream music, unfortunately you don't own it at all"
slides.notes: Students find the four disadvantages in the book first.

slides.body:
Page 132, Exercise 3

QuestionWhich points does the conclusion contain?
AnswerOne advantage, and the writer's opinion.
ExplanationIt repeats the convenience of streaming, then gives the opinion.
Transcript"even though I like the convenience of streaming, ... I still prefer downloads."
slides.notes: The conclusion does not add new ideas. It repeats and decides.

slides.title: Strategy: Take a position
slides.body:
DoChoose one side.
WhyYour essay ends with your opinion.
HowThink about your own experience.
slides.notes: Emphasize: no side is wrong, but you must choose one.

slides.title: Try it: Choose a side
slides.body:
Teacher example: Weekend homework
The teacher must choose a side.
 Homework helps you remember the lesson.
 Weekends are for rest and family.
slides.notes: Ask: which side would the teacher choose? Then click.

slides.title: Try it: Choose a side
slides.body:
Teacher example: Weekend homework
The teacher must choose a side.
 Homework helps you remember the lesson.
✓Weekends are for rest and family.
slides.notes: The teacher chose the second side. Everyone can choose differently.

slides.title: Your topic card
slides.body:
Read your question twice.

Find the technology.

Think of advantages and disadvantages.

Choose your side.
slides.notes: Distribute the topic cards now. Students work alone. Monitor.

slides.title: State your position
slides.body:
OpinionI am for …
I am against …
ReasonOne reason is …
EvidenceFor example, …
slides.notes: These frames start every good response.

slides.title: Write your response
slides.body:
Write your opinion. Add one reason. Add one example.

Use your topic card. Three sentences.
slides.notes: Three sentences minimum. Timer: five minutes. Collect the responses.

slides.title: Give Your Opinion
slides.body:
OpinionI am against weekend homework.
ReasonOne reason is weekends are for rest.
EvidenceFor example, students need time with family.

Opinion — Reason — Evidence
slides.notes: Pairs share their responses using the frames.

slides.title: Your essay starts here
slides.body:
You read the task. You chose your side.

Next lesson: we plan the essay.
slides.notes: Collect the responses. Preview lesson 2: planning on pages 133–134.
